children: Japanese Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi and Mongolian President Ukhnaa Khurelsukh on Thursday confirmed that the two countries have reached a substantial agreement on the expansion of Chinggis Khaan International Airport using yen-denominated loans.
With the move, the two governments aim to improve air connectivity between Japan and Mongolia. Motegi and Khurelsukh held a meeting in Ulaanbaatar that lasted about 40 minutes.

Mongolia is a landlocked country sandwiched between China and Russia, so it prioritizes relationships with the two countries. However, it is also trying to deepen relations with "third neighbors" such as Japan. Japan is Mongolia's largest aid donor, with cumulative yen loans totaling over 182.9 billion yen.

During the meeting, Motegi and Khurelsukh reaffirmed the importance of a 2022 joint statement, which confirmed the commitment of the two countries to issues such as freedom, democracy, the rule of law and the free and open Indo-Pacific initiative. Motegi stated that Japan will be Mongolia's "most important" third neighbor. "We will support Mongolia in reinforcing its autonomy and resilience," he said.

The two leaders also agreed to further strengthen cooperation toward regional peace and stability. Mongolia is the final stop of a four-country tour by Motegi that began Aug. 29. He is scheduled to wrap up his itinerary on Friday and return to Japan.
